account: This morning I read my appointment book and yesterday's office record at town hall. No new correspondence has arrived. My next appointment is the mill's grain inspection at ten; afterward I have lunch at home, council letters at one, dockside tea at three, office at four-thirty, and home at seven. Freight came to ask about transport work: his warehouse is empty, the ferry is at the east landing, and no town deliveries or spending are authorized. I will ask at the mill whether transport is needed. The builder reports the west workshop, school and residential roads are passable, with no confirmed defects; his earlier east-route and crossing-lamp checks also found nothing requiring repair. He reports no costs or materials used and a zero repair estimate. He wants any future repairs agreed as an itemized fixed price before work, payable after inspected completion. The one unusual matter is his report of a child's vague remark about a bridge change. I have not heard the child or verified the claim. The builder plans to ask the baker; I requested prompt reporting of any confirmed hazard. I heard the baker talking and shouting earlier but could not understand the words, so I cannot connect that to the bridge remark. The secretary is keeping the records and receiving visitors. So far this appears to be routine town business and efforts to find or arrange work, with an unresolved bridge rumor rather than evidence of damage or any hidden purpose.
